checks: Source 915016d15b315b1b:01–02 gives the same prescribed rays and areas, block test and singular-case polynomial limits. The numerical search for a different inverse-weight implication is outside the candidate claim.

Exact determinants of all six pairs of consecutive and next-neighbor canonical directions equal one. Substitution of scaled determinants in the accepted criterion simplifies its diagonal to the stated ell_i and its off-diagonal to -h_i.
Fixing x_1 and x_4 disconnects the remaining variables into the indicated two path blocks. Direct two-by-two inversion gives the written minimizers and reduced diagonal and mixed coefficients.

Under the positive-definite path hypothesis the Schur criterion is equivalent to PSD and therefore to polygon realization. Since gamma is nonnegative, taking absolute endpoint values preserves a negative witness and the minimizing interior entries then are nonnegative.

If all h_i are positive, a singular feasible path block would give a null vector whose zero extension is in the kernel of the whole PSD matrix, contradicting the two adjacent positive edges. The proof handles singular paths separately via L+eta I and continuous polynomials, without a geometric approximation claim.
Multiplying the reduced matrix by the product of path determinants gives F,-J,G; evaluating it at (B,b) gives the last required necessary condition.
